name: Volcanic field
notes: Primary succession on lava, ash and cinder: nitrogen-fixing pioneer shrubs, tough grasses and mosses/lichens on bare rock, with ohia and birch/willow scrub where soil forms. Drawn on Hawaii (Kilauea/Mauna Loa), Iceland (Hekla, Surtsey), Mt St Helens, Etna and Mt Fuji.

canopy.name: Ohia lehua
canopy.source: Metrosideros polymorpha, ohia lehua, first tree to colonise fresh Hawaiian lava, red flowers, 3-25 m — Wikipedia / USFS

canopy.name: Downy birch
canopy.source: Betula pubescens, downy birch, only native forest tree of Iceland, colonising old lava fields, 4-15 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Etna broom tree
canopy.source: Genista aetnensis, Mount Etna broom, tree-broom endemic to Etna lava flows, 3-10 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Lodgepole pine
canopy.source: Pinus contorta, lodgepole pine, pioneer conifer on pumice plains of Cascades volcanoes (Mt St Helens, Crater Lake), 10-30 m — Wikipedia / USDA

canopy.name: Japanese larch
canopy.source: Larix kaempferi, Japanese larch, pioneer conifer on volcanic scoria of Mt Fuji and central Honshu, 10-30 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Volcanic pioneer shrub
shrub.source: Vaccinium reticulatum, ohelo, pioneer berry shrub on fresh Hawaiian cinder and lava, 0.3-1.5 m — Wikipedia / USFS

shrub.name: Tea-leaved willow
shrub.source: Salix phylicifolia, tea-leaved willow, colonist scrub on Icelandic lava and ash, 1-4 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Fuji knotweed
shrub.source: Reynoutria (Fallopia) japonica, Japanese knotweed, primary coloniser of volcanic scoria slopes on Mt Fuji, 1-3 m — Wikipedia (Hirose & Tateno)

shrub.name: Etna soapwort
shrub.source: Astragalus siculus, spiny cushion milkvetch endemic to high Etna lava slopes, 0.2-0.6 m — Wikipedia / Etna Park

shrub.name: Pumice lupine
shrub.source: Lupinus lepidus, prairie lupine, nitrogen-fixing pioneer that led recovery on Mt St Helens pumice plain, 0.1-0.4 m — Wikipedia / USGS

shrub.name: Sea buckthorn
shrub.source: Hippophae rhamnoides, sea buckthorn, nitrogen-fixing thorny shrub planted/naturalised on Icelandic and Eurasian volcanic gravels, 1-5 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Lava moss
ground.source: Racomitrium lanuginosum, woolly fringe-moss, grey moss carpet covering Icelandic lava fields — Wikipedia

ground.name: Lyme grass
ground.source: Leymus arenarius, sea lyme grass, sand-binding pioneer on Icelandic black ash and Surtsey, 0.5-1.5 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Swordfern
ground.source: Nephrolepis exaltata, Boston/sword fern, colonises cracks in young Hawaiian pahoehoe lava, 0.3-1 m — Wikipedia / USFS

ground.name: Amaumau fern
ground.source: Sadleria cyatheoides, amau fern, small tree fern with red new fronds, pioneer on Kilauea lava — Wikipedia / USFS

ground.name: Fireweed
ground.source: Chamaenerion angustifolium, fireweed, first colonist on Mt St Helens ash and Icelandic tephra, 0.5-2 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Map lichen
ground.source: Rhizocarpon geographicum, map lichen, yellow-green crust on bare basalt worldwide — Wikipedia
